prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, by bifunctional PROTACs and by thalidomide-type molecular glues that recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system through cereblon

statement.case_for: Four of eight of us put B023 first independently, and I think the reason is that it is the clearest case of a new chemical modality in the pool. A designed small molecule brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase, which converts occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven degradation and makes targets without a conventional binding pocket reachable. The mechanism is chemically explicit (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design, the cereblon degron and its molecular-glue logic). The concept has been reproduced by many independent groups over two decades, and many degraders are in clinical trials. My three names cover the two halves that cannot be separated: Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept and first demonstrations, and Handa for identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target. That second half explains why a long-used drug works and it makes the glue strand a mechanistic discovery, not just a medicinal-chemistry one.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader is approved, so the therapeutic payoff is still forward-looking, and a prize now could be called early. The credit problem is real: Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim all have strong claims, and any three-person cut leaves out someone decisive. The prize also joins two strands, PROTACs and molecular glues, that grew from different discoveries and could be argued to be two prizes. If the committee judges maturity strictly by approved drugs, B061 or B021 may be safer.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B023 first but would put Ciulli in the trio with Crews and Deshaies, arguing that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structural work turned PROTACs into a general, drug-like platform; he treats the cereblon work as secondary.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli point seriously: the structural and physical-organic work on VHL and ternary complexes is the best chemistry in this field. But I would still put Handa ahead of him. Without cereblon, thalidomide, lenalidomide and pomalidomide, which are approved drugs, remain empirical, and glues are the only part of this field with proven clinical benefit. Ciulli's work refined the PROTAC design, whereas Handa's identified a target and a mechanism, so I would take Handa over Ciulli if only three places are available. I would accept Ciulli's omission as a real cost and say so in the citation, which I made mechanism-based so that it does not depend on one lineage.

responses.point: Zou ranks B023 only fourth. She thinks it is scientifically well confirmed but that recognition could be premature because approved drugs are still lacking, and she puts Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling first as a mature, enabling synthetic tool.
responses.response: I disagree on timing. The thalidomide/cereblon half already has years of approved-drug use in myeloma, so clinical validation is not hypothetical, and the PROTAC half is supported by independent reproducibility and trials. Our committee has honoured mechanism and concept ahead of approvals before. On B002, I agree it is excellent chemistry, but I share Aqvist's own reservation that it is a later chapter of the palladium cross-coupling story honoured in 2010, which makes it a lower priority than a new modality. I would not oppose B002 as a second part, but I think Zou's maturity bar for B023 is set higher than we apply elsewhere.

responses.point: Sparr ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first as a physical-chemistry achievement with huge demonstrated impact, and ranks B023 only seventh.
responses.response: The impact of B041 is not in doubt and I ranked it fifth, but I think it is the weaker prize in chemistry terms. The Vancouver ionizable-lipid and remote-loading work is real, but credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is crowded and entangled with patents. And because the 2023 Medicine prize honoured the mRNA side, the delivery vehicle can be seen as an enabling technology to a prize already awarded. The case for B023 in comparison is that the chemical idea and the mechanistic discovery are both clean and attributable to a small group.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks proton-coupled electron transfer (B028) first as a unifying physical-chemical concept spanning enzymes and electrocatalysis, and puts B023 third because clinical validation is still emerging.
responses.response: As someone working on ribonucleotide reductase, a radical enzyme in which PCET is central, I accept that B028 is conceptually deep and textbook-level. My reservation is only that it is supported by one member, has the narrowest opening support on the shortlist, and has a credit problem among Meyer, Mayer, Nocera and Hammes-Schiffer that I cannot judge better than Brzezinski can. If he can show that the theory-versus-molecular-systems split is settled, I would read B028 as a serious second candidate. I also share his concern about clinical maturity but weigh it less, for the reasons given to Zou.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli should replace Handa, or the prize should be split into a PROTAC part and a separate molecular-glue part with different names.
Whether the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader should delay recognition for one more year.
Whether B061 (base editing) is viewed as overlapping with the 2020 genome-editing prize, which would affect my first alternative.
My knowledge of the individual contributions is from memory and not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work on ribonucleotide reductase and dNTP metabolism is thematically near some biochemistry here, but I have no recorded personal or institutional tie to any person on the shortlist, including Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Liu, Hyman, Brangwynne or Rosen.
